 Olymel opens $142 million integrated plant in Quebec
 

 New facility quadruples production capacity for pork and poultry

 

 
 
 
 
 28 September 2026
 
 

 
 
 
 1 minute read
 
 

 
 
 
 By: Global Ag Media 
 

 

 
 
 
 
 North America

 

 

 

 

 Olymel officially inaugurated its new integrated plant in Trois-Rivières last week, marking the completion of one of the largest modernisation projects in the company's history, according to the company. The $142 million project significantly expanded the plant and upgraded it into a state-of-the-art facility.

With an annual production capacity of 50 million kilograms, more than four times its original capacity, the plant now handles pork and poultry processing, slicing, and packaging all under one roof. In addition to La Fernandière sausages and hams, the plant now produces the vast majority of Olymel's deli meats sold across the country.

"Today, we're celebrating the successful completion of a key project for Olymel and recognizing the exceptional work of our teams and many partners," said Daniel Rivest, CEO of Olymel. "They worked tirelessly for over 15 months to bring this high-tech facility to life, and I'm very proud of that. Thanks to them, we're now better equipped to serve our customers in Canada and around the world."

The Trois-Rivières plant incorporates innovative technologies in energy efficiency, automation, and artificial intelligence, supporting Olymel's commitment to reducing operations-related greenhouse gas emissions by 25% by 2030. New equipment includes an industrial battery system, described as an industry first in Canada, that stores energy during low-demand periods and releases it during peak demand to reduce strain on the Hydro-Québec power grid. Other innovations include a shift toward water-based over air-based cooking, heat recovery, closed-loop water management, and reduced transportation.

The project was announced in June 2025, with the first new production lines phased in last May. The plant was expanded from 51,700 to 137,200 square feet, nearly 2.5 times its original size, and roughly 100 jobs have been created, bringing the total workforce to about 400 employees.

The project generated $110 million in orders placed with Canadian companies, including more than $94 million with local businesses in the Mauricie region. Energy efficiency initiatives at the plant are expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 3,000 tonnes of CO₂ equivalent per year.

More than $20.3 million in financial assistance was provided by public-sector partners, including a $15 million loan from Investissement Québec, $2 million from MAPAQ, a $1.8 million grant from Hydro-Québec, $1.3 million from Quebec's Ministère de l'Environnement, and $250,000 from the Ville de Trois-Rivières.

translationZh:
Olymel上周正式为位于Trois-Rivières的新一体化工厂举行落成典礼，公司称这标志着其历史上最大现代化项目之一完成。该项目投资1.42亿美元，大幅扩建了工厂并升级为最先进的设施。

该工厂年产能达5000万公斤，是原有产能的四倍多，如今在同一屋檐下完成猪肉和禽肉的加工、切片和包装。除了La Fernandière香肠和火腿外，该工厂现在还生产Olymel在全国销售的大部分熟食肉制品。

Olymel首席执行官Daniel Rivest表示：“今天，我们庆祝Olymel一个关键项目的成功完成，并表彰我们团队和众多合作伙伴的卓越工作。他们为让这座高科技设施落地而不懈努力了超过15个月，我对此感到非常自豪。正因为有他们，我们现在更有能力服务加拿大及全球客户。”

Trois-Rivières工厂融合了能源效率、自动化和人工智能方面的创新技术，支持Olymel到2030年将运营相关温室气体排放减少25%的承诺。新设备包括一套工业电池系统，被称为加拿大行业首创，可在低需求时段储存能量，并在高峰需求时释放，以减轻Hydro-Québec电网压力。其他创新还包括从空气烹饪转向水基烹饪、热回收、闭环水管理和减少运输。

该项目于2025年6月宣布，首批新生产线于去年5月分阶段投入使用。工厂从51,700平方英尺扩建至137,200平方英尺，约为原规模的2.5倍，并创造了约100个工作岗位，使总员工人数达到约400人。

该项目向加拿大公司下达了1.1亿美元订单，其中超过9400万美元给了Mauricie地区的本地企业。工厂的能源效率举措预计每年减少3,000吨二氧化碳当量的温室气体排放。

公共部门合作伙伴提供了超过2030万美元的财政援助，包括Investissement Québec的1500万美元贷款、MAPAQ的200万美元、Hydro-Québec的180万美元赠款、魁北克环境部的130万美元，以及Trois-Rivières市的25万美元。
